thread:
maria gonzalez: hey everyone :wave: finishing up day 1, running into a couple devbox issues. macbook M1 Ventura, followed the quickstart (brew + asdf) but `asdf install nodejs 18.16.0` fails with gpg verification errors. also the dotfiles bootstrap didn't create `~/.config/redwood/env` — the repo install passed but symlinks look incomplete. any quick tips?

tom ellis: welcome aboard! :tada: for nodejs + asdf on mac you usually need gpg and to import the release keys. run: `brew install gpg` then `~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring`. after that `asdf install nodejs 18.16.0` should work.

alex chen: +1 to tom. also check you have `brew` in your PATH before asdf runs — sometimes the bootstrap uses `which gpg` and fails. if it still errors paste the exact failure here.

maria gonzalez: thanks — the import step was missing. after `brew install gpg` the import script hung on a keyserver until I CTRL-C'd, then retried with `--keyserver hkps://keys.openpgp.org` and it finished. node installed.

alex chen: nice. about dotfiles: did you clone our dotfiles and run `./bootstrap.sh`? that script symlinks into `~/.config/redwood` and prompts to create `env.example` -> copy to `env` and fill secrets.

maria gonzalez: I ran bootstrap but it skipped env because env.example already existed. I copied it but not sure which keys are required. what's the minimal set to start the API locally?

tom ellis: minimal dev env: `REDWOOD_API_KEY`, `DB_URL` (sqlite path is ok for local), `AWS_REGION` only if you use S3 features. you can run without real secrets for most front-end work. i'll paste the tiny snippet you can use:```
# ~/.config/redwood/env
REDWOOD_API_KEY=dev-local-key
DB_URL=file://$HOME/.local/redwood/dev.sqlite3
LOG_LEVEL=debug
```

maria gonzalez: perfect, added that and `yarn dev` starts. quick follow-up: asdf plugins for python & terraform — any pinned versions we prefer?

tom ellis: we pin python to 3.11.6 for infra tests, terraform 1.5.7 for infra repo. run: `asdf plugin-add python && asdf install python 3.11.6` and `asdf plugin-add terraform && asdf install terraform 1.5.7`.

alex chen: FYI the workstation checklist (internal wiki) has a short bootstrap checklist and common gotchas: https://redwood.internal/devex/workstation-checklist — includes Rosetta step if you need it on M1 for some brew bottles.

dev-onboard-bot: Reminder: please sign the CLA and complete the security training to get full repo access — https://redwood.internal/onboarding.

maria gonzalez: thanks all — resolved the main blockers. last thing: docker permissions complaining when running tests (socket permission denied). any simple workaround?

tom ellis: run Docker Desktop x86 on M1? Usually `sudo chown $USER:staff /var/run/docker.sock` during local dev fixes it, but prefer adding your user to the docker group if using linux. On mac Docker Desktop manages the socket, so restart Docker Desktop after bootstrap.

maria gonzalez: fixed with restart. everything green now. appreciate the quick help :heart:
